description: Documents the precedence rule between error and constraint_violations, raised by @MSKazemi (MSKazemi/aobench#51#discussioncomment-18405164, point 3): the two fields' denominator semantics directly contradict each other -- error means the row produced nothing usable and consumers reasonably drop it, while invalidates_result=true means the row MUST still count toward summary.total. A producer can emit both (e.g. an agent that breaches scope and then times out mid-answer). This document is deliberately schema-valid -- the combination is a SHOULD NOT for producers, not a hard schema-level MUST NOT, since a real (if discouraged) producer bug or edge case shouldn't make an otherwise-parseable document unparseable -- but the spec is explicit about the resolution: error wins, because 'no usable result was produced' is upstream of 'the result broke a rule' -- you cannot invalidate the scoring of something that was never scored. A consumer reading this document MUST treat this row as errored, not as a disqualified-but-scored result, regardless of the constraint_violations entry present alongside it.

error.message: Agent did not produce a final answer within the 30s task budget after the scope breach was recorded.

constraint_violations.detail: Agent invoked a tool outside the requesting role's allowed_tools before the run subsequently timed out mid-answer.
